nodes.name: FeCo-LDH arrays growth
nodes.procedure: FeCo-LDH arrays grown using Ni foam (NF) as substrate using mixed-solvent strategy.
nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Fig. 1(a), the RuxSACs@FeCo-LDH is formed by first growing FeCo-LDH arrays using Ni foam (NF) as a substrate

nodes.name: Ru1 single-atom doping
nodes.procedure: In situ growth of Ru single-atomic-site on the FeCo-LDH arrays using mixed-solvent strategy with different molar ratios of Ru precursors denoted as Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH.
nodes.source_text: followed by in situ growth of an Ru single-atomic-site on the FeCo-LDH arrays... denoted as Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH (Table S1, ESI)

nodes.name: Ru2 single-atom doping
nodes.procedure: In situ growth of Ru single-atomic-site on the FeCo-LDH arrays using mixed-solvent strategy with different molar ratios of Ru precursors denoted as Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH.
nodes.source_text: RuxSACs@FeCo-LDH with different molar ratios of the Ru precursors is constructed and denoted as Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH

nodes.description: OER performance in O2-saturated 1.0 M KOH (three-electrode)

stability_CV_cycles.value: 20000 cycles, 10 mV overpotential increase at 1000 mA/cm^2

nodes.source_text: Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH exhibits... ultralow overpotential of 194 and 230 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm^-2... Tafel slope of 25 mV dec^-1... 246 mV at 1 A cm^-2... current density of 1 A cm^-2 only decreases by 5% over 1200 h... overpotential only decreases by 10 mV after 20 000 continuous cycles

Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH... superior HER activity... Tafel slope as low as 53 mV dec^-1... overpotentials of 84 and 117 mV at 500 mA cm^-2 and 1 A cm^-2... maximum exchange current density... largest C_dl of 328 mF cm^-2... smallest R_ct of 0.92 Ω... negligible loss of overpotential at 1 A cm^-2 over 1000 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH (anode in Ru1||Ru2 electrolyzer)
nodes.source_text: assembled an alkaline electrolyzer with Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH as anode and Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH as cathode... requires 1.47 and 1.52 V at 500 and 1000 mA cm^-2... nearly 100% faradaic efficiency... negligible decay over 1000 h at 1 A cm^-2

nodes.source_text: OER performance of Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH in alkaline simulated seawater (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl)... overpotential required is just 260 and 268 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm^-2

performance_note.value: some activity decay due to pollutants

nodes.source_text: in alkaline natural seawater (1 M KOH + seawater) electrolytes... exhibits some activity decay due to the pollutants in natural seawater

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH contains Fe ~0.236 wt%, Co ~0.450 wt%, Ru ~0.508 wt%; Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH contains Fe ~0.013 wt%, Co ~0.009 wt%, Ru ~1.532 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: using ICP analysis, the contents of Fe, Co, and Ru for Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH are ∼0.236, ∼0.450 and ∼0.508 wt% respectively, and the contents of Fe, Co, and Ru for Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH are ∼0.013, ∼0.009 and ∼1.532 wt% respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH maintains uniform 3D porous structure of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets with smooth surface and sharp edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) images reveal that Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH still maintain the uniform 3D porous structure composed of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets with a smooth surface and sharp edges.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright dots marked by yellow circles correspond to single Ru atoms anchored on the (107) plane of FeCo-LDH; reveals interface symmetry breaking structure with asymmetric Fe/Co interfaces containing defective segments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the observed bright dots (marked by yellow circles in Fig. 1(d)) correspond to single Ru atoms... anchored on the (107) plane of the FeCo LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH nanosheets have ultrathin thickness of 3.09 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1(f) reveals the ultrathin nature of Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH nanosheets, with a thickness of only 3.09 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, and Ru species in Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy further demonstrates the homogeneous distribution of the Fe, Co, and Ru species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms Fe(III) species; Co binding energy negatively shifts by 0.65 eV compared to FeCo-LDH indicating higher electron density; higher Ru 3p binding energy suggests oxidized Ru x+ species; lattice oxygen binding energy shifts to 530.2 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical peaks of Fe(III) corresponding to Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH were confirmed... the binding energy of the Co species on Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH negatively shifts by approximately 0.65 eV... the higher binding energy of the Ru 3p suggests the presence of oxidized Ru x+ species... the binding energy for lattice oxygen of Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH shifts to a lower level (530.2 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge pre-edge peaks at ≈7133.2 eV indicate atomically dispersed Fe~+3; Fe K-edge shifts to lower energy confirming Ru–O–Fe structure; Co K-edge between CoO and Co3O4 (valence +2 to +3); Ru K-edge between Ru foil and RuO2 (oxidation state 0 to +4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge XANES spectra of Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH and FeCo-LDH samples show distinct pre-edge peaks at ≈7133.2 eV... the absorption edge of these samples is close to that of Fe2O3, indicating that the atomically dispersed Fe species carry a positive charge of ∼+3... the Ru K-edge XANES spectra of Ru1 SACs@FeCo-LDH and Ru2 SACs@FeCo-LDH... reveal that the edge energy is between the Ru foil and RuO2

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe–O peak at R=1.5 Å, no Fe–Fe scattering; Co–O peak at 1.6 Å, no Co–Co scattering; Ru–O peak, no Ru–Ru bond confirms single-atom dispersion of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Fourier transforms of the EXAFS spectra (FT-EXAFS...) of the Fe element reveal a peak at R=1.5 Å which corresponds to the Fe–O scattering... For the Ru x SACs@FeCo-LDH has no scattering peak of the Ru–Ru bond whereas it is the main peak for Ru foil, indicating that no Ru–Ru bond exists.
